parameters.content:
## Reconcile a Google Sheets roster against Discord roles and report the drift

Your volunteer list, course cohort or club membership lives in a Google Sheet, and the Discord roles drift away from it within a week. Every Monday this reads the sheet, reads the server, and reports the gap. It is read only against Discord, so you can point it at a live 4,000 member server and it cannot break anything.

### How it works
1. A weekly schedule fires and `Set Reconcile Settings` supplies every ID, URL and tuning value from one node.
2. `Get Guild Roles` fetches the server's roles live, so you configure role NAMES and never copy a role ID.
3. `Read Roster Sheet` pulls the roster and `Normalize Roster Rows` flags any row that cannot be judged instead of guessing at it.
4. `Get Server Members` pulls every member with their role IDs, paginating natively.
5. `Reconcile Roster Against Discord` joins the two on `discord_user_id` and sorts every mismatch into a named bucket.
6. One row per mismatch is appended to the report tab, then the two headline counts are posted to a channel.

### Setup steps
- [ ] Create a Discord application, add a bot to it, and invite that bot to your server.
- [ ] Switch on the SERVER MEMBERS INTENT for the bot in the Discord developer portal. Reading members returns nothing without it.
- [ ] Add the Discord Bot credential to both Discord nodes and to `Get Guild Roles`.
- [ ] Put your server ID, report channel ID, roster sheet URL and report sheet URL into `Set Reconcile Settings`.
- [ ] Set `gated_roles` to the role names you want checked, comma separated, spelled as they appear in Server Settings.
- [ ] Give the roster tab the columns `discord_user_id`, `display_name`, `entitled_role`, and optionally `status`.
- [ ] Give the report tab the header row `checked_at`, `run_id`, `bucket`, `discord_user_id`, `display_name`, `discord_username`, `role`, `note`.
- [ ] Run it once by hand and read the drift report before you trust the counts.

### Customization
`active_status_values` and `inactive_status_values` decide which roster statuses count as entitled, and a status in neither list is reported rather than assumed. `grace_period_days` stops recent joiners being flagged before anyone has had a chance to give them their role. `ignore_user_ids` keeps bots and service accounts out of the report.

## Configure once, then read both sides

Every ID, URL and tuning value lives in `Set Reconcile Settings`. Role IDs are fetched live from the guild, so you type role NAMES and there is no snowflake to typo or to go stale when somebody renames a role.

## Diff the roster against Discord

A row whose `status` matches neither the active nor the inactive list is reported as unjudgeable, never quietly treated as inactive. Recent joiners inside the grace period are named separately rather than counted as drift.

## Report two numbers, not three lists

The post leads with the two counts a coordinator can act on. Every count comes from the reconcile step, so the channel post and the sheet can never disagree.

nodes.name: Note Your Sheet Needs User IDs

parameters.content:
## Your sheet needs Discord user IDs
The join runs on discord_user_id, so the roster has to hold 18 digit Discord snowflakes. Nobody hand maintains a column of those, and once it decays the report starts crying wolf.

To read one: Discord settings, Advanced, switch on Developer Mode, then right click a member and choose Copy User ID.

Capture the ID at signup rather than backfilling it later. Add the field to your intake form and the column keeps itself current.

Rows with a blank or malformed ID are not dropped quietly. They land in the report as roster_row_unusable and are counted on their own line in the channel post.

## Reads the member list, and nothing else
This workflow never calls roleAdd or roleRemove and there is no fix it branch. It reads members, writes a sheet, and posts a message, so it is safe to point at a production server.

The one hard blocker is the SERVER MEMBERS INTENT. In the Discord developer portal open your application, go to Bot, and switch on Server Members Intent. For a bot in fewer than 100 servers that is a toggle you flip yourself, not an approval queue, but the member list comes back empty until you do. The bot also has to be invited to the server first.

Bots that hold a gated role will show up as no_roster_row. Put their user IDs in ignore_user_ids to keep the report clean.
